2-dimensional table T(i, j) defined for any integers i and j, read by antidiagonals in the southeast quadrant. T(i, j) gives the "Fibonacci depth" of (i, j): form the Fibonacci sequence starting with i, j: w(0) = i, w(1) = j, w(n) = w(n-1) + w(n-2). It can be shown that for all but finitely many n, the w(n) have the same sign, i.e., are all positive, all negative or all zero. T(i, j), is the smallest number of iterations required to find out which of these cases holds.

Let S be the sequence generated by these rules: 0 is in S, and if z is in S, then z * (1+i) and (z-1) * (1+i) + 1 are in S (where i denotes the imaginary unit), and duplicates are deleted as they occur; a(n) = the real part of the n-th term of S.
a(n) = number of steps to reach a prime when x -> sigma(x)-1 is repeatedly applied to 2^n-1, or -1 if no prime is ever reached.
a(1) = 1, a(r(n)^k) = 1 + k * a(n) where r(n) is the n-th number that is not a perfect power A007916(n).
G.f.: Re(1/(i*x; x)_inf), where (a; q)_inf is the q-Pochhammer symbol, i = sqrt(-1).
Restricted growth sequence transform of A278222(A292383(n)); a filter related to runs of numbers of the form 4k+3 encountered on trajectories of A005940-tree.
a(n) is the number of odd primes in the sequence [n, floor(n/2), floor(n/4), ..., 1].
First differences of A293230: how many more alive nodes there are in generation n+1 than in generation n in the binary tree of persistently squarefree numbers.
a(n) = Sum_{k=1..n} sign(omega(n+1) - omega(n)) (where omega(m) = A001221(m), the number of distinct primes dividing m).
Number of dying nodes (withering branches) at generation n in the binary tree of persistently squarefree numbers (A293230).
Minimum of the number of primes appearing among the smaller parts and the number of primes appearing among the larger parts of the partitions of n into two parts.
The tree of Farey fractions (or the Stern-Brocot tree), read across rows (the fraction i/j is represented as the pair i,j).
a(n) is the least value of pi(n*m) - pi(n)*pi(m) for any positive m <= n.
a(n) = pi(n-1) - pi(floor(n/2)), where pi is A000720.
Number of partitions of n into generalized octagonal numbers (A001082).
Number of divisors of n that are in A257691.

Let S be the sequence of integer sets defined by the following rules: S(0) = {0}, S(1) = {1} and for any k > 0, S(2*k) = {2*k} U S(k) and S(2*k+1) = {2*k+1} U S(k) U S(k+1) (where X U Y denotes the union of the sets X and Y); a(n) = the number of elements of S(n).
Number of partitions of 2*n-1 into four squares.
a(n) = 1 + the number of distinct earlier terms that are coprime to n.
Number of partitions of n into two distinct parts such that the larger part is nonsquarefree.
Initial digit of the number of partitions of n.
Binary weight of the contents of node n in Doudna-tree (A005940).
Number of primes of the form 4*k+3 <= 4*n+3.
Number of toothpicks added at n-th stage to the toothpick structure of A296610.
Number of iterations of A220096 required to reach 0 starting from n.
Number of pieces in the list d(m), d(m-1), ..., d(0) of base-3 digits of n; see Comments.
a(n) is the number of connected components in the graph with vertices 1..n and adjacency criterion i and j not coprime.
Decimal expansion of lim_ {n->oo} (s(0) + s(1) + ... + s(n) - (n + 1)*g), where g = (1 + sqrt (5))/2, s(n) = (s(n - 1) + 1)^(1/2), s(0) = 2.
Triangle read by rows: Independent domination number for rectangular queens graph Q(n,m), 1 <= n <= m.
Number of 3's in the n-th {2,3}-power tower; see Comments.
For x=n, iterate the map x -> Product_{k is a prime dividing x} (k + 1), a(n) is the number of steps to see a repeated term for the first time.
Number of ways to write n^2 as x^2 + y^2 + z^2 + w^2 with x >= y >= 0 <= z <= w such that x or 2*y is a power of 4 (including 4^0 = 1) and x + 15*y is also a power of 4.
Number of skew partitions whose quotient diagram is connected and whose numerator is the integer partition with Heinz number n.

Consider a spiral on an infinite hexagonal grid. a(n) is the number of cells in the part of the spiral from 1st to n-th cell that are on the same column or diagonal (in any of three directions) as the n-th cell along the spiral, including that cell itself.
a(n) = Sum_{1 <= i <= j <= n} mu(i*j)*floor((n/i)/j).
A sequence based on the period 6 sequence A151899.
Real part of the n-th Gaussian prime x + i*y, x >= y >= 0, ordered by norm x^2 + y^2.
Number of strict integer partitions of n in which the even parts appear as often at even positions as at odd positions.
Nearest integer to mean of first n primes.
Decimal expansion of an analog of the Landau-Ramanujan constant for Loeschian numbers.
a(n) = k if n can be written as the sum of the factorials of k distinct positive integers. Otherwise, a(n) = 0.
Largest integer k such that n^2 - 3*2^k can be written as x^2 + 2*y^2 with x and y integers, or -1 if no such k exists.
Number of rooted twice-partitions of n where the first rooted partition is constant and the composite rooted partition is strict, i.e., of type (Q,R,Q).
Number of distinct subset-products of the integer partition with Heinz number n.
Analog of A056239 for nonstandard factorization based on the sieve of Eratosthenes (A083221).
T(n,k)=Number of nXk 0..1 arrays with every element equal to 0, 1 or 3 horizontally, diagonally or antidiagonally adjacent elements, with upper left element zero.
Irregular triangle read by rows in which row n lists all parts of all partitions of n, in nondecreasing order.
T(n,k)=Number of nXk 0..1 arrays with every element equal to 0, 1, 3 or 4 horizontally, diagonally or antidiagonally adjacent elements, with upper left element zero.
T(n,k)=Number of nXk 0..1 arrays with every element equal to 0, 1, 3 or 5 horizontally, diagonally or antidiagonally adjacent elements, with upper left element zero.
a(n) is the least k such that k * A005277(n) is a term of A002202.
T(n,k)=Number of nXk 0..1 arrays with every element equal to 0, 1, 4 or 5 horizontally, diagonally or antidiagonally adjacent elements, with upper left element zero.
T(n,k)=Number of nXk 0..1 arrays with every element equal to 0, 1, 3 or 6 horizontally, diagonally or antidiagonally adjacent elements, with upper left element zero.
T(n,k)=Number of nXk 0..1 arrays with every element equal to 0, 1, 4 or 6 horizontally, diagonally or antidiagonally adjacent elements, with upper left element zero.
Restricted growth sequence transform of ordered pair [Q(n-Q(n-1)), Q(n-Q(n-2))], the left & right summand of Hofstadter Q-sequence A005185.
T(n,k)=Number of nXk 0..1 arrays with every element equal to 0, 1, 3, 4 or 5 horizontally, diagonally or antidiagonally adjacent elements, with upper left element zero.
Number of ways to write prime(n)^2 as x^2 + 2*y^2 + 3*2^z with x,y,z nonnegative integers.
Maximum number of 6's possible in an infinite Minesweeper grid with n mines.
Maximum number of 7's possible in an infinite Minesweeper grid with n mines.
T(n,k)=Number of nXk 0..1 arrays with every element equal to 0, 1, 3, 4 or 6 horizontally, diagonally or antidiagonally adjacent elements, with upper left element zero.
Number of numbers < n whose binary representation has the same difference between the numbers of 0's and 1's as n does.
T(n,k)=Number of nXk 0..1 arrays with every element equal to 0, 1, 3, 5 or 6 horizontally, diagonally or antidiagonally adjacent elements, with upper left element zero.
List of middle divisors: for every positive integer that has middle divisors, add its middle divisors to the sequence.
T(n,k)=Number of nXk 0..1 arrays with every element equal to 0, 1, 4, 5 or 6 horizontally, diagonally or antidiagonally adjacent elements, with upper left element zero.
Number of ways to write n as a*(2*a-1) + b*(2*b-1) + 2^c + 2^d, where a,b,c,d are nonnegative integers with a <= b and c <= d.
T(n,k)=Number of nXk 0..1 arrays with every element equal to 0, 1, 3, 4, 5 or 6 horizontally, diagonally or antidiagonally adjacent elements, with upper left element zero.
Break up the list of values of the divisor function d(k) into nondecreasing runs; sequence gives lengths of successive runs.
Number of bits in binary expansion of A294994(n).
Number of ways to write n as a*(a+1)/2 + b*(b+1)/2 + Bell(k) + Bell(m) with 0 <= a <= b and 0 < k <= m, where Bell(k) denotes the k-th Bell number A000110(k).
Number of ways to write 2*n+1 as p + 3^k + 5^m, where p is a prime, and k and m are nonnegative integers.
Number of ways to write 2*n as p + 2^k + 5^m with p prime and 2^k + 5^m squarefree, where k and m are nonnegative integers.
Number of ways to write 2*n as p + 2^k + 5^m with p prime and 2^k + 5^m a product of at most three distinct primes, where k and m are nonnegative integers.
Restricted growth sequence transform of A246277(A098550(n)), related to indices in the prime factorization of Yellowstone permutation.
Restricted growth sequence transform of A046523(A098550(n)), a filter sequence based on the prime signature of the Yellowstone permutation.
Number of primitive inequivalent oblique sublattices of rectangular lattice of index n.
Number of integers k > 1 such that n - F(k) is a positive squarefree number, where F(k) denotes the k-th Fibonacci number A000045(k).
Number of nonnegative integers k such that n - F(k)*F(k+1) is positive and squarefree, where F(k) denotes the k-th Fibonacci number A000045(k).
Number of partitions (d1,d2,...,dm) of n such that d1/1 >= d2/2 >= ... >= dm/m and 0 < d1 <= d2 <= ... <= dm.
Number of partitions (d1,d2,...,dm) of n such that d1/1 > d2/2 > ... > dm/m and 0 < d1 <= d2 <= ... <= dm.
Restricted growth sequence transform of A304759(n), formed from 1-digits in ternary representation of A048673(n).
Size of the largest subset of the cyclic group of order n which does not contain a nontrivial 3-term arithmetic progression.
Number of ways to write n as the sum of a positive tribonacci number (A000073) and a positive odd squarefree number.
Number of integer partitions of n whose distinct parts are pairwise indivisible.
Restricted growth sequence transform of A305295(n), formed from 1-digits in ternary representation of A245612(n).

Square array A(n,k), n > 0 and k > 0, read by antidiagonals, with initial values A(1,k) = k and recurrence equations A(n+1,k) = A(n,k) for 0 < k <= n and A(n+1,k) = A(n,k) - A000035(n+k) for 0 < n < k.
Square array read by antidiagonals upwards in which row k has k as its first term and each subsequent term is the least possible value such that the sum of any 2 or more terms does not equal a prime.
Expansion of Product_{r not a perfect power} 1/(1 - x^r).
Order of rowmotion on the divisor lattice for n.
Restricted growth sequence transform of A278233, filter-sequence for GF(2)[X]-factorization.
Number of ways to write n as w + x^5 + pen(y) + pen(z), where w is 0 or 1, and x,y,z are integers with x >= w and pen(y) < pen(z), and where pen(m) denotes the pentagonal number m*(3*m-1)/2.
Number of ways to write n as w + x^4 + y*(y+1)/2 + z*(z+1)/2, where w is 0 or 1, and x, y, z are nonnegative integers with x >= w and y < z.
Number of terms of the set of divisors of n that are not the product of any other two distinct divisors.
Consider the numbers in A024796, numbers expressible in more than one way as i^2 + j^2 + k^2, where 1 <= i <= j <= k; sequence number of ways these numbers can be expressed.
Number of partitions of n into 2 distinct prime powers (not including 1).
Number of ways to write n as u^2 + 2*v^2 + 3*x^2 + 4*y^2 + 5*z^2, where u,v,x,y,z are generalized pentagonal numbers (A001318).
Determinant of the circulant matrix whose first column corresponds to the binary digits of n.
Inverse of the Hardy-Ramanujan asymptotic partition function.
Square array T(n,k), n > 0, k > 1, read by antidiagonals: T(n, k) = 1 when n <= 2 or k <= 2, T(n, k) = T(n-T(n-1, k-1), k-T(n-2, k-2)) + T(n-T(n-2, k-2), k-T(n-1, k-1)) otherwise.
Number of ways of breaking the binary expansion of n into consecutive blocks with no leading zeros.
a(n) is the number of different types of faces of Johnson solid J_n, with solids ordered by indices in Johnson's paper.
a(n) is the minimum number of iterations of the form x -> x + x^j (where j is a nonnegative integer and need not be identical in each iteration) required to reach n starting from 1.
Number of partitions of n into 3 mutually distinct, mutually nonadjacent prime parts.
Number of partitions of n into 3 prime powers (not including 1).
Smallest k > 1 such that A014574(n)*k is adjacent to a prime.
Counterclockwise square spiral constructed by greedy algorithm such that the product of the values of any two vertically or horizontally adjacent cells is unique.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of positive terms such that for any distinct m and n, a(m) * a(m+1)^2 <> a(n) * a(n+1)^2.
Number of integer-sided triangles with perimeter n and sides a, b, and c such that a <= b <= c and a|b.

Let EM denote the Ehrenfeucht-Mycielski sequence A038219, and let P(n) = [EM(1),...,EM(n)]. To compute EM(n+1) for n>=3, we find the longest suffix S (say) of P(n) which has previously appeared in P(n). Suppose the most recent appearance of S began at index n-t(n). Then a(n) = length of S, while t(n) is given in A308175.
Number of irreducible Egyptian fractions of denominator n which are the sum of 2 unit fractions.
Limiting row sequence of the array A128628.
Number of ways to write n as 6^i + 3^j + A008347(k), where i, j and k > 0 are nonnegative integers.
a(n) is the number of k > 0 such that n-1-2*k > 0 and the points (n-1-2*k, a(n-1-2*k)), (n-1-k, a(n-1-k)) and (n-1, a(n-1)) are aligned.
Least k > 0 such that A014222(k) == A014222(k+1) (mod n).
Least k > 0 such that A114561(k) == A114561(k+1) mod n.
Index of A053319(n) in A014574; -1 if it doesn't exist.

a(n) is the number of tiles of a chosen color on the front side of the Rubik Cube after n repetitions of the following procedure: rotate the right side by a 1/4 turn clockwise, then rotate the whole cube around the front-back axis by a 1/4 turn clockwise.
Maximum sum of base lengths over all minimal factorizations of length-n binary strings.
The analog of A309077(n), but allowing fractional powers.
The sum of the number of times each unique digit in the previous number occurred in the numbers before that with a(1) = 0.
If a(n) is not a term of a(0..n-1), then a(n+1) = a(n) - a(n - a(n)); otherwise a(n+1) is the number of terms equal to a(n) in a(0..n-1). Start with a(0)=0, a(1)=0.
Number of even parts appearing among the second largest parts of the partitions of n into 4 parts.
Decimal expansion of the imaginary part of the square root of 1 + i.
a(n) is the least base b in the range 2..n where the product of the digits of n is maximized.
An example of a morphically imprimitive word.
a(n) = a(phi(n)) + a(n-phi(n)) with a(1) = a(2) = a(3) = 1.
Number of ways to represent 8*n + 4 as the sum of four distinct odd squares.
a(n) is the rank of the multiplicative group of Gaussian integers modulo n.
Writing the integers of the sequence in English produces a word-sequence that spells itself (see the Example section).
a(n) is the number of open intervals (m, m+1) containing at least one fraction n/k, where m and k are integers between 1 and n.
a(n) is the number of k with 1 <= k <= n-1 such that a(k) + 2 * a(n-k) <= n.
Number of distinct values of X*(3*X-1) mod n.
Number of positions in the n-th free pure symmetric multifunction (with empty expressions allowed) with one atom.
Number of partitions of n into a prime and two positive squares.
Number of decimal places to which the n-th convergent of the continued fraction expansion of Khintchine's constant matches the correct value.
Sum of elements of the multiset spanning an initial interval of positive integers with multiplicities equal to the prime indices of n in weakly decreasing order.
Number of conjugacy classes of the Sylow 2-subgroup of the alternating group on n letters.
Number of integer partitions of n whose sum of reciprocals squared is an integer.
For any n >= 0 with binary expansion Sum_{k=0..w} b_k * 2^k, let f(n) = Sum_{k=0..w} b_k * i^k * 2^floor(k/2) (where i denotes the imaginary unit); a(n) is the imaginary part of f(n).

For any n >= 0 with base-9 representation Sum_{k=0..w} d_k * 9^k, let g(n) = Sum_{k=0..w} s(d_k) * 3^k (where s(0) = 0, s(1+2*j) = i^j and s(2+2*j) = i^j * (1+i) for any j > 0, and i denotes the imaginary unit); a(n) is the imaginary part of g(n).
Restricted growth sequence transform of A318836.
Number of divisors d of n for which 2*phi(d) > d.
Number of integer partitions of n whose parts all have the same number of prime factors, counted with multiplicity.
Irregular triangle where T(n,k) is the number of permutations of the integer partition with Heinz number A215366(n,k).
Sum of prime indices of the n-th squarefree number.
Digits of one of the three 7-adic integers 6^(1/3) that is related to A319097.
Number of trailing zero entries in row n of triangle A319411.
Take the Zeckendorf representation of n (A014417(n)), drop least significant bit, take the inverse Zeckendorf representation.
Number of distinct Eisenstein primes in the factorization of n.
Total number of factors in a factorization of n into Eisenstein primes.
a(n) is the rank of the multiplicative group of Eisenstein integers modulo n.
Number of partitions of n into exactly two nonzero decimal palindromes.
Sum of digits when n is represented in phitorial (A001088) base.
Number of strict T_0 integer partitions of n.

Let f(1) = 1, f(2) = 1 + i (where i denotes the imaginary unit), f(3) = 2 + i, and for n > 2, f(n+1) is the Gaussian integer in the first quadrant (with positive real part and nonnegative imaginary part) with least modulus and sharing at least one prime factor with f(n-1) but none with f(n) (in case of a tie, minimize the imaginary part); a(n) = the real part of f(n).
Maximum number that can be obtained by iteratively adding or multiplying together parts of the integer partition with Heinz number n until only one part remains.
a(n) is the number of integer partitions of n with largest part <= 4 for which the index of the seaweed algebra formed by the integer partition paired with its weight is 0.
a(n) is the number of integer partitions of n with largest part <= 5 for which the index of the seaweed algebra formed by the integer partition paired with its weight is 0.
Number of product-sum knapsack partitions of n. Number of integer partitions y of n such that every product of sums of the parts of a multiset partition of any submultiset of y is distinct.
a(n) = a(n-1-a(a(a(n-1)))) + a(a(a(a(n-1)))) for n > 1, a(n) = n for n < 2.
Number of partitions of n into distinct parts such that the successive differences of consecutive parts are decreasing.
Two-column table read by rows: The Mayan 260-day Tzolkin cycle, with day names replaced by numbers.
Number of partitions of n such that the successive differences of consecutive parts are nonincreasing, and first difference <= first part.
Expansion of (1 + x^5) / ((1 - x^2) * (1 - x^3) * (1 - x^7)) in powers of x.
For p the n-th prime congruent to 1 (mod 4), a(n) is the clique number of the quadratic residue (Paley) graph over F_p, the field of order p.

For p the n-th prime congruent to 1 (mod 4), a(n) is the clique number of the subgraph of the quadratic residue (Paley) graph over F_p, the field of order p, that is induced by the set of vertices that are themselves quadratic residues.
a(0) = 0, a(n) is the number of x such that a(x) = a(n-1) and there exists no y such that x < y < n and a(y) > a(n-1).
Let p = prime(n); a(n) = number of pairs of primes (i,j) with i < j < p such that i*j == 1 (mod p).
Maximum number of unbordered conjugates for a binary word of length n.

Let S be the sequence of integer sets defined by these rules: S(1) = {1}, and for any n > 1, S(n) = {n} U S(pi(n)) U S(n - pi(n)) (where X U Y denotes the union of the sets X and Y and pi is the prime counting function); a(n) = the number of elements of S(n).
Number of partitions of n into consecutive parts, all singletons except the largest.
a(n) is the maximum value of k such that A007504(k) <= prime(n).

For any sequence f of positive integers, let g(f) be the unique Golomb-like sequence with run lengths given by f and let k(f) be the unique Kolakoski-like sequence with run lengths given by f and initial term 1; this sequence is the unique sequence f satisfying f = g(k(f)).
Irregular triangle read by rows where T(H(u),H(v)) is the coefficient of m(v) in h(u), where H is Heinz number, m is monomial symmetric functions, and h is homogeneous symmetric functions.
a(n) = Pi(12,5)(n) + Pi(12,7)(n) - Pi(12,1)(n) - Pi(12,11)(n) where Pi(a,b)(x) denotes the number of primes in the arithmetic progression a*k + b less than or equal to x.

Tetrangle where T(n,H(u),H(v)) is the coefficient of m(v) in h(u), where u and v are integer partitions of n, H is Heinz number, m is monomial symmetric functions, and h is homogeneous symmetric functions.
a(n) = number of primes of the form p = n - q, where q is a prime or semiprime.
a(n) = number of primes of the form p = 2n - q, where q is a prime or semiprime.
Minimal number of steps needed to get from n to 1, where for n > 1 the next step is to either n-1 or max(a,b) for any a > 1 and b > 1 such that ab=n.
Irregular triangular array read by rows: T(n,k), n>=1, is the number of ordered factorizations corresponding to each unordered factorization, indexed by k.
Number of integer partitions of n whose parts all have the same number of prime factors (counted with multiplicity) and whose product of parts is a power of a squarefree number (A072774).
Number of integer partitions of n whose parts all have the same number of prime factors (counted with or without multiplicity) and whose product of parts is a squarefree number.
Lexicographically earliest such sequence a that a(i) = a(j) => A285330(i) = A285330(j) for all i, j.
Lexicographically earliest such sequence a that a(i) = a(j) => A048675(i) = A048675(j) for all i, j.
From Goldbach's conjecture: a(n) is the number of decompositions of 6n into a sum of two primes.
Number of iterations of A049820(x) = x - A000005(x) needed to reach an odd number or zero, when starting from x = 2n.
Lexicographically earliest such sequence a that for all i, j, a(i) = a(j) => f(i) = f(j), where f(1)=0, and f(n) = A252463(n) for n > 1.
Number of strict integer partitions of n using numbers that are not perfect powers.
Number of strict integer partitions of n using 1 and numbers that are not perfect powers.
Nested square root sqrt(b(n) + sqrt(b(n-1) + ... + sqrt(b(1))...)), where b(n) = A323635(n).
a(n) is the number of primes p such that A007504(n) <= p < A007504(n+1).
a(0) = 1, followed by pairs (multiplicity of rarest term, value of that term). Choose the least value of rarest term if there is a tie.
k appears t+1 times, where t is the number of trailing zeros in A324474(k).
k appears t+1 times, where t = A364377(k) is the number of trailing zeros in the greedy Jacobsthal representation of k, A265747(k).
Numerator of fractional part of average number of bit toggles to reach n as defined in A324495. The denominator is given in A324497.
Decimal expansion of a constant related to the asymptotics of A306729.
Number of divisors d of n such that A323243(d) is either 0 or 1 (mod 4).
a(n) is the binary length of A324876(n).
Binary length of A324866(n), where A324866(n) = A156552(n) OR (A323243(n) - A156552(n)).
Number of distinct factors in the factorization of n into factors q(i) = prime(i)/i, i > 0.
a(n) = the number of values of m such that the sum of proper unitary divisors of m (A034460) is n.
Sum of sums of the multisets of prime indices of each prime index of n.
a(1) = 1; a(n) = number of prime factors of n counted with multiplicity plus the largest prime index of n.
Number of integer partitions of n whose augmented differences are weakly increasing.
Number of integer partitions of n whose k-th differences are strictly decreasing for all k >= 0.
Irregular triangle whose rows are the sorted combined parts of all strict integer partitions of n.
Number of length-3 integer partitions of n whose largest part is not greater than the sum of the other two.
Number of distinct frequencies in the frequency span of n.
Reading the first row of this array or its successive antidiagonals is the same as reading this sequence.
Weight of the set-system with BII-number n.
Number of maximal primitive subsets of {1..n}.
Number of divisors of n that are reachable from n with some combination of transitions x -> gcd(x,sigma(x)) and x -> gcd(x,phi(x)).

Let f(n) be a sequence of distinct Gaussian integers such that f(1) = 0 and for any n > 1, f(n) = f(floor(n/2)) + k(n)*g((1+i)^(A000120(n)-1) * (1-i)^A023416(n)) where k(n) > 0 is as small as possible and g(z) = z/gcd(Re(z), Im(z)); a(n) is the real part of f(n).

Let f(n) be a sequence of distinct Gaussian integers such that f(1) = 0 and for any n > 1, f(n) = f(floor(n/2)) + k(n)*g((1+i)^(A000120(n)-1) * (1-i)^A023416(n)) where k(n) > 0 is as small as possible and g(z) = z/gcd(Re(z), Im(z)); a(n) is the imaginary part of f(n).
Expansion of Sum_{k>=1} x^k * (1 + x^(2*k)) / (1 - x^(3*k)).
Number of maximal subsets of {1..n} such that no two elements have the same sorted prime signature.
Number of maximal subsets of {1..n} containing no quotients of pairs of distinct elements.
Number of strict factorizations of 2^n into factors > 1 with integer average.
Langton's ant with three cell colors: number of gray cells after n moves of the ant.
a(0) = 0; a(1) = 0; for n > 0, a(n) = the sum of the number of times each digit in a(n-1) has occurred from a(0) to a(n-2) inclusive.
a(0)=0; for n > 0, a(n) is the number of distinct digit strings that occur at least twice (not counting overlapping occurrences) in the concatenation of all previous terms.
Maximum vertex-degree of the set-system with BII-number n.
The number of monomials in a strong elliptic divisibility sequence t_n in free variables x, y, z.
Number of odd prime powers <= n (with exponents > 0).
Number of connected divisors of n.
